title: Trace-distance characterization of recurrent pairwise synchronization in cavity-coupled superconducting qubits
abstract: We theoretically investigate recurrent pairwise synchronization in three super?conducting qubits coupled to a common single-mode microwave cavity. The qubits interact indirectly through the cavity field and are driven by a coher?ent microwave field. We obtain the coherent dynamics in the dressed-state basis and quantify pairwise synchronization by the trace distance between reduced single-qubit density matrices. The trace-distance dynamics exhibit oscillatory wave-packet structures, with low-trace-distance regions identifying finite syn?chronization windows. An envelope-threshold procedure is introduced to extract the representative duration of these windows. By varying the middle-qubit coupling strength and the relative coupling ratio of the outer qubits, we con?struct a parameter-dependent map of the synchronization-window duration. The duration decreases rapidly with increasing relative outer-qubit coupling and becomes weakly dependent on the middle-qubit coupling in the stronger-coupling regime. These results provide a reduced-state-based characterization of coherent collective dynamics in multiqubit circuit-QED systems.
summary: This theoretical study characterizes recurrent pairwise synchronization in three superconducting qubits coupled via a microwave cavity. By using the trace distance between reduced single-qubit density matrices, the authors quantify synchronization windows. They map the duration of these windows, finding that the duration is highly sensitive to the relative outer-qubit coupling ratio.
main_problem: The paper investigates how to characterize recurrent pairwise synchronization in a three-qubit system coupled to a microwave cavity.
main_result: The duration of synchronization windows is found to decrease rapidly with increasing outer-qubit coupling ratio but becomes weakly dependent on the middle-qubit coupling in the strong-coupling regime.
method:
The authors use the trace distance between reduced single-qubit density matrices, $D_{\mu
u}(t)$, to quantify pairwise asynchronization, employing an envelope-threshold procedure to extract window durations.
model_or_system: The system consists of three superconducting qubits (L, M, R) coupled to a common single-mode microwave cavity (circuit-QED). The dynamics are solved in the dressed-state basis using the full Hamiltonian.
key_observables:
Pairwise asynchronization quantified by the trace distance $D_{\mu
u}(t)$, and the representative duration ($\Delta t$) of synchronization windows.
important_parameters: Middle-qubit coupling strength ($\eta_M$) and the relative outer-qubit coupling ratio ($\lambda = \eta_L / \eta_M = \eta_R / \eta_M$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on truncating the cavity mode to $|0angle$ and $|1angle$, and the synchronization window duration is defined by the maximum time separation between high-trace-distance wave packets.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup (three qubits coupled to a cavity), the raw oscillatory wave-packet structure of the trace distance, and parameter maps showing the dependence of the extracted synchronization window duration ($\Delta t$) on coupling strengths.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the Hamiltonian and the trace-distance measure. It then details the dressed-state time evolution and the envelope-threshold procedure for window extraction. Finally, it presents the parameter-dependent map of the synchronization window duration, analyzing the trends with varying coupling strengths.
why_interesting: This work provides a reduced-state-based, quantitative diagnostic tool (trace distance) to study coherent collective dynamics in circuit-QED systems, complementing entanglement measures and offering insights into how coupling geometry dictates synchronization timescales.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic illustration of three superconducting qubits coupled to a common single-mode microwave cavity. The middle qubit is fixed at a field antinode, while the two outer qubits are symmetrically positioned and their cavity couplings can be varied through their positions.
Figure 2: Time evolution of DLM(t) and DMR(t) for ηM/2π = 300 MHz and λ = 0.2. The blue and red curves represent DLM(t) and DMR(t), respectively.

Figure 3: Illustration of the envelope-threshold method for extracting the synchronization-window duration. The original trace-distance signal Dµν(t) is shown in blue, and the smoothed envelope Eµν(t) is shown in orange. The adaptive threshold Dth separates the high-trace-distance wave packets from the low-envelope regions. The highlighted interval ∆t is the duration of a low-trace- distance synchronization window.

Figure 4: Synchronization-window duration as a function of the coupling configuration. (a) Parameter-dependent map of the representative duration ∆t obtained from DLM(t) as a func- tion of the relative coupling ratio λ = ηL/ηM = ηR/ηM and the middle-qubit coupling strength ηM/2π. The color scale represents ∆t in microseconds. (b) Representative line cuts of ∆t as a function of λ for ηM/2π = 300, 350, 400, 450, and 500 MHz.
